title: Agent-first analysis roadmap: raw mapping, bounded inspection, diagnostics, and workflow features
description:
# binscout — agent analysis roadmap

Date: 2026-10-15. Repository: `/Users/mimi/work/rsdbg`.
Implementation progress: **0/17 steps complete (0%)**. Planning and backlog creation are not implementation.
Beads: epic **`rsdbg-0vt`**, children **`rsdbg-0vt.1`–`rsdbg-0vt.17`**. Child suffix matches the numbered step below. All implementation issues are open; no work is claimed or implemented. The graph has 31 blocking edges in addition to parent-child links.

Planning complete: current code/backlog reviewed, duplicate checks performed, user decisions recorded, detailed issues created, and dependency ordering recorded. Ready first: **`rsdbg-0vt.1`** (contracts) and **`rsdbg-0vt.2`** (mapping-aware cache identity).

## Current state

`binscout` 0.3.0 is a Rust 2024 library with JSON CLI and 13 stdio MCP tools. It loads ELF/PE/Mach-O/LE/raw binaries, discovers functions and CFGs, extracts strings and xrefs, emits a deliberately minimal IR, and saves analysis plus annotations in a redb sidecar. Synthetic integration tests cover format parsing, budgets, stale snapshots, query bounds, and both interfaces.

`Project::open_raw` supports base, architecture, and entry, but CLI/MCP openers do not expose those settings. `Analysis::blocks_page` and `block_insns` already exist, whereas `Project::func_detail` serializes the whole function. Analysis documents missing indirect edges and heuristic function ownership; MCP tools reopen and rebuild the project on every call. Existing completed work, including LE support (`rsdbg-jix`) and human-readable IR coverage (`rsdbg-jbw.1`), must not be duplicated or reopened.

## Confirmed decisions

- Include all six proposed features and all three accompanying improvements.
- Prioritize raw mapping, bounded inspection, and diagnostics.
- Breaking CLI/MCP schemas are allowed, with explicit before/after migration documentation and regression tests. Permission is not a mandate to churn unrelated endpoints.
- Investigate indirect-control-flow recovery before selecting one implementation pattern.
- Only this plan and beads state are changed in plan mode. Implementation requires build mode.

## Assumptions and scope boundaries

- Continue as a headless, local, agent-first static analyzer; no GUI, dynamic execution, decompiler, symbolic executor, additional architecture, or new binary format in this roadmap.
- Preserve one JSON value on CLI stdout, existing exit-code conventions, hex/decimal address parsing, dual numeric/hex output addresses, and no writes to the analyzed binary.
- Proposed API/command names below are design targets; step 1 records the final schema contract before adapters are implemented.
- Explicit raw mapping is opt-in: CLI `--raw --arch ARCH --base ADDR [--entry ADDR]`; MCP optional `raw: {arch, base, entry?}` on binary-taking tools. Architecture and base are required in explicit raw mode; no flags preserves existing auto-detection/default fallback. Raw-only options without raw mode are errors. Accepted architectures match the existing five modes.
- A raw mapping is one contiguous existing `RawOptions` mapping, not a multi-segment firmware configuration language. Entry must be in the mapped range, with alignment appropriate to the selected mode; base-plus-length arithmetic is checked.
- Query pages retain the 1024-row maximum. New operation budgets below are initial explicit design limits, not claims about current constants.
- Annotation interchange is JSON returned by CLI/MCP and supplied as a bounded input document; no arbitrary server-side output-path writer is added. Shell redirection may save CLI output when the user executes the command in build mode.
- Import uses exact binary and mapping identity, with no force/rebase option in v1. Use a cryptographic digest for portable identity (SHA-256; a focused new dependency may be needed); the current 64-bit cache hash is not sufficient as an integrity check for interchange.
- Performance changes are conditional on measurements. No session cache, concurrency rewrite, or speedup promise is preapproved by this plan.
- Proprietary `_testdata/` binaries remain optional local oracles, never CI dependencies or tracked fixtures. Existing untracked `_testdata/` is left untouched.

## Plan

Each checkbox corresponds to exactly one beads issue. Each step is one logical change, including its directly associated tests. No implementation is done yet.

### 1. [small] Freeze the next JSON/CLI/MCP contract (P1)
- [ ] Define the feature schemas and deliberate breaking changes.
- **What/where:** update `docs/book/src/json-protocol.md` with page envelope `{total, offset, limit, next_offset, items}`, deterministic address ordering, zero-limit/end-of-list behavior, address encodings, input validation, and a protocol revision distinct from database schema and crate version. Document mappings for new CLI/MCP names in their reference chapters. Prefer one consistent page model for new views and intentionally revised function inspection; do not normalize unrelated strings/symbols endpoints just for style.
- **Why:** keep CLI and MCP consistent and prevent accidental breakage while changing large-function output. Exact counts describe the filtered result; `next_offset` is null when exhausted or limit is zero.
- **Verify:** schema examples cover empty, zero-limit, clipped-limit, and final pages; reviewed before steps 3, 5, 7, 10, or 12. Existing exit/error contracts remain explicit.

### 2. [medium] Make snapshot reuse mapping-aware (P1)
- [ ] Include effective loader configuration in cache identity.
- **What/where:** `src/db.rs`, `src/lib.rs`, and `src/loader.rs`: identity includes binary content, auto-versus-explicit-raw mode, raw arch/base/entry, and analysis revision. Validate before rebuilding cached layouts. Bump/migrate the sidecar schema as necessary. Same bytes with different options must never reuse layouts; no-options and explicit-raw opens must not accidentally alias.
- **Annotations:** preserve existing stale-content behavior for unchanged mapping, but reject reuse of a populated annotation sidecar under an incompatible mapping with an actionable separate-DB error. Do not silently move annotations to new addresses. Legacy snapshots whose mapping cannot be established are rebuilt, not trusted; ambiguous legacy raw annotations require a separate DB.
- **Why:** exposing `open_raw` broadly without this guard risks interpreting cached analysis with the wrong architecture or address space.
- **Verify:** new `tests/raw_mapping.rs` and `tests/stale_cache.rs` cases vary only architecture/base/entry/mode, test legacy handling, retain same-mapping annotation behavior, and assert reads never save or create sidecars.

### 3. [medium] Expose explicit raw mapping through both interfaces (P1)
- [ ] Thread validated raw options through every binary-taking operation.
- **What/where:** `src/cli.rs`, `src/mcp.rs`, `src/lib.rs`, `src/loader.rs`: use the contract above and one shared validated opener/options parser rather than endpoint-specific interpretation. Respect default or explicit DB paths. Report effective mode, arch, base, and entry in project information.
- **Why:** support firmware/raw ARM/Thumb workflows using the engine already present.
- **Verify:** `tests/raw_mapping.rs`, `tests/cli.rs`, `tests/mcp.rs`: equivalent x86-32, AArch64, ARM32, and Thumb synthetic mappings give matching addresses; existing x86-64 mode remains covered. Test missing/unknown options, unmapped/misaligned entries, overflow, and unchanged no-flags container detection. Explicit raw mode must not fall back to a different mode after failure.
- **Depends on:** 1, 2.

### 4. [medium] Add bounded core function views (P1)
- [ ] Separate function summary, block pages, and instruction pages.
- **What/where:** `src/lib.rs`, existing helpers in `src/analysis.rs`, new `tests/function_pages.rs`: implement compact function metadata (entry/name/counts and call count, not unbounded call arrays), deterministic block summaries, and a paged block-instruction query. Resolve interior function addresses consistently; require the selected block to belong to that function. Avoid constructing the full function JSON before slicing.
- **Why:** existing internal page helpers can provide bounded responses without redesigning the engine.
- **Verify:** a synthetic function with more than 1024 instructions/pages reconstructs identically from successive pages, with no gaps/duplicates; limit zero/overflow-sized limit/out-of-range offsets behave as specified; unknown function/block reports NotFound. Per-page cloned/serialized rows scale with the selected page, not whole-function size.
- **Depends on:** 1.

### 5. [medium] Route CLI/MCP function inspection through bounded views (P1)
- [ ] Make compact `func` the default and expose `blocks` and `block_insns`.
- **What/where:** `src/cli.rs`, `src/mcp.rs`, `tests/cli.rs`, `tests/mcp.rs`: `func BINARY ADDR` returns compact metadata; `blocks BINARY ADDR --offset --limit` and `block-insns BINARY ADDR BLOCK --offset --limit` map to MCP `blocks`/`block_insns`. Keep full CFG export explicitly requested via existing `cfg`, rather than embedding it in `func`; document that CFG export can still be large.
- **Why:** a default tool call should not dump an entire large function. This is an intentional breaking response change; no hidden compatibility/full-output switch is required.
- **Verify:** CLI/MCP page values agree; `func` contains no instruction arrays; new tools appear in MCP discovery; large-function requests stay within row bounds; errors retain existing channel/exit semantics. Check byte-size sanity on the synthetic stress fixture without claiming row limits are a universal byte limit.
- **Depends on:** 3, 4.

### 6. [large] Capture and persist analysis diagnostics and discovery provenance (P1)
- [ ] Retain evidence about how analysis was obtained and where it is incomplete.
- **What/where:** `src/analysis.rs`, `src/disasm.rs` only if needed to retain typed control-flow facts, `src/db.rs`, `src/lib.rs`, new `tests/diagnostics.rs`: record discovery reasons (entry/export/direct-call/prologue), unresolved indirect jump/call sites, and decode failures encountered during discovery. Reasons can coexist and must be sorted/deduplicated. Provenance is evidence, not a fabricated confidence percentage or proof of correct boundaries.
- **Bounds/persistence:** cap diagnostic records at 100,000 per project; on diagnostic-cap exhaustion continue analysis and expose `diagnostics_truncated` plus omitted count. Existing hard analysis budgets still return Error::Limit rather than masquerading as successful partial analysis. Persist diagnostics/reasons with an analysis revision; old caches must reanalyze rather than manufacture a clean diagnostic set. Do not log every undecoded byte or build an unbounded event history.
- **Why:** callers need to distinguish known gaps, failed decodes, and heuristic seeds from verified analysis.
- **Verify:** synthetic direct/indirect/invalid/prologue cases produce exact reason/site records; valid termination is not a decode failure; deterministic fresh/cache round-trips agree; diagnostic-cap boundary behavior is explicit; tests assert unsupported control flow is not silently upgraded to a proven edge.
- **Depends on:** 2.

### 7. [medium] Expose paged diagnostics and provenance (P1)
- [ ] Add discoverable, bounded diagnostic queries and compact completeness metadata.
- **What/where:** `src/lib.rs`, `src/cli.rs`, `src/mcp.rs`, `tests/diagnostics.rs`, `tests/cli.rs`, `tests/mcp.rs`: `diagnostics` CLI/MCP query filtered by kind and optional containing function; use the page contract. Add reason sets to compact function metadata, and diagnostic totals/truncation/analysis revision to project info. Do not equate zero retained diagnostics with proof of complete recovery.
- **Why:** make the engine's limitations actionable without flooding each normal tool response.
- **Verify:** filtering precedes pagination; CLI/MCP return identical records; reasons survive rename and snapshot reopen; invalid filters are errors; querying does not write a sidecar.
- **Depends on:** 1, 5, 6.

### 8. [medium] Publish machine-readable IR coverage (P2)
- [ ] Distinguish implemented lift mappings from semantic completeness.
- **What/where:** `src/ir.rs`, `src/lib.rs`, `src/cli.rs`, `src/mcp.rs`, `tests/ir.rs`, `tests/addr_hex.rs`: add an `ir_coverage` library query and CLI `ir-coverage`/MCP `ir_coverage` accepting architecture without opening a binary. Return implemented opcode families, explicit unknown/partial status, and limitations (operand strings, flags, stack/calling-convention effects, no SSA/PHI production). Add per-range counts for decoded/lifted/unlifted instructions based on actual lift results and a bounded mnemonic summary.
- **Why:** extends completed human-readable coverage work (`rsdbg-jbw.1`), rather than duplicating it or claiming decompiler semantics. Real NOP and unlifted fallback NOP must remain distinguishable.
- **Verify:** tests cover genuine NOP versus fallback warning, mapped-but-partial semantics, all five modes, and consistency between advertised families and representative positive/negative lifts. No second drifting list of individually supported mnemonics if family dispatch can share metadata.
- **Depends on:** 1.

### 9. [medium] Implement bounded byte-pattern search in the core (P2)
- [ ] Search mapped, file-backed bytes using literal bytes and `??` wildcards.
- **What/where:** new `src/search.rs`, `src/lib.rs`, new `tests/byte_search.rs`: parse whitespace-separated full-byte tokens (e.g. `48 8B ?? ??`), reject empty/all-wildcard/odd/invalid patterns, and cap pattern length at 4096 bytes. Support section and half-open VA-range filters; return VA/hex, file offset where available, section, and match length. Include overlapping matches, use stable VA ordering, and never bridge gaps or separate mappings; suppress duplicate representations of the same match in overlapping section views.
- **Bounds:** scan at most 256 MiB of unique file-backed mapped bytes per request, with explicit Error::Limit rather than silent truncation. Do not materialize virtual BSS. Cap result pages at 1024 and skip/materialize matches lazily; an exact total may require a full bounded scan. Use a literal anchor plus verification instead of expanding wildcards to regex or an accidental unbounded quadratic scan.
- **Why:** support locating instruction signatures and binary structures without adding execution or patching.
- **Verify:** literal/wildcard/overlap/page-boundary matches, filters, raw mapping, invalid tokens, BSS/gap behavior, arithmetic bounds, and budget edges. Compare against a simple bounded reference matcher over randomized small buffers.
- **Depends on:** 1, 2.

### 10. [small] Expose byte search in CLI/MCP (P2)
- [ ] Add `search-bytes` / `search_bytes` with shared filters and page envelopes.
- **What/where:** `src/cli.rs`, `src/mcp.rs`, `tests/cli.rs`, `tests/mcp.rs`: pattern, section, range start/end, offset/limit, and common raw/DB options. No regex/nibble wildcard language, external signature database, or file-writing result export.
- **Why:** make the core search useful from both supported interfaces.
- **Verify:** exact CLI/MCP parity on synthetic PE/raw patterns; malformed patterns and unmapped ranges return documented errors; repeated queries never create/write sidecars; discoverability schema includes all filters.
- **Depends on:** 3, 9.

### 11. [medium] Add validated, atomic annotation interchange (P2)
- [ ] Define versioned JSON export and all-or-nothing import.
- **What/where:** new `src/annotations.rs`, `src/lib.rs`, `src/db.rs`, `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock` if SHA-256 support is added, new `tests/annotation_transfer.rs`: export format revision, SHA-256, binary length, effective mapping, and sorted nonempty `{addr, rename?, comment?}` rows. Exclude host paths and analysis snapshots. Import validates the entire document before one write transaction; rename targets must be known entries, comments retain the any-address contract. Reuse field/row/storage caps; cap serialized interchange documents at 16 MiB in both directions, reject duplicate addresses, malformed identity, and unsupported revisions. Oversized export fails explicitly rather than emitting a document the importer cannot accept or silently truncating annotations.
- **Merge policy:** default fails on differing existing field values; equal values are idempotent. Explicit `overwrite` replaces supplied fields only; absent fields leave existing values unchanged; empty strings clear supplied fields. Untouched annotations remain. Whole-set replace/rebase/force import is out of scope.
- **Why:** preserve valuable analyst work independently of the disposable analysis cache without partial imports or cross-binary corruption.
- **Verify:** export/import/reopen round-trip, exact identity mismatch, raw mapping mismatch, duplicate rows, oversized input/text, unknown rename, comments outside mapped memory, conflict/overwrite/clear semantics, idempotence, and failure in the last row leaving DB and in-memory annotations unchanged. Export is read-only.
- **Depends on:** 2.

### 12. [medium] Expose portable annotations through CLI/MCP (P2)
- [ ] Add export/import operations without arbitrary server-side output paths.
- **What/where:** `src/cli.rs`, `src/mcp.rs`, `tests/cli.rs`, `tests/mcp.rs`: CLI `annotations-export BINARY` emits one JSON document; `annotations-import BINARY --input PATH [--overwrite]` reads capped JSON and returns counts. MCP `annotations_export` returns the document and `annotations_import` accepts the document plus optional overwrite. Common binary/raw/DB options apply. Enforce MCP serialized document/row/text limits before transaction; check rmcp input-allocation limitations and document any transport-level residual risk.
- **Why:** support backups/sharing while keeping analyzed binaries immutable and stdout machine-readable.
- **Verify:** CLI export can be imported into a fresh DB; MCP equivalent produces the same annotations; invalid final row/conflict yields no partial write; tool schemas, runtime error behavior, and hash/mapping validation match the core.
- **Depends on:** 1, 3, 11.

### 13. [medium] Benchmark repeated MCP investigation workflows (P2)
- [ ] Establish reproducible costs before choosing an optimization.
- **What/where:** new `tests/mcp_workflow_perf.rs` (ignored/manual measurements, not flaky timing gates), new `docs/book/src/performance.md`, `docs/book/src/SUMMARY.md`: deterministic synthetic small and large fixtures, cold/no-sidecar, saved-sidecar/new-process, and repeated same-process scenarios. Measure `project_info → functions → func → blocks → block_insns → xrefs → strings`, with fixture size/counts, compiler/platform, wall time distribution, response bytes, and peak RSS where available. Separate file read/hash, layout replay, analysis, and serialization using minimal measurement hooks only if external measurements cannot isolate them.
- **Why:** cache-hit opens still replay layouts, but the dominant cost and useful optimization are not yet established. Do not assume page-cache-warm equals in-memory-project reuse.
- **Verify:** release-build run command is documented; at least five measured repetitions after warm-up; fresh and cached functional outputs agree; no claimed speedup without before/after data; measurements and tool availability limitations are recorded, not encoded as arbitrary CI deadlines.
- **Depends on:** 5 (the workflow uses new bounded tools).

### 14. [small] Decide the smallest justified MCP optimization (P2)
- [ ] Record a go/no-go decision from step 13 rather than prebuilding a cache.
- **What/where:** update the performance chapter and this plan with the measured bottleneck and proposed bounded solution, or explicitly conclude no optimization is justified. If a resident-project cache is proposed, specify eviction/memory budget, binary+mapping identity, external annotation invalidation, rename/comment coherence, DB lock lifecycle, and runtime/cancellation behavior before an implementation issue is approved. A raw-size or mtime-only cache key is insufficient.
- **Why:** avoid trading correctness, memory bounds, and cross-process freshness for unproven speed.
- **Verify:** decision cites reproducible measurements and unchanged observable results; any proposed implementation has quantified acceptance criteria and a separate follow-up issue. This task is complete with a justified no-go; this roadmap does not promise an optimization implementation.
- **Depends on:** 13.

### 15. [medium] Investigate one conservative jump-table pattern (P3)
- [ ] Establish whether one indirect jump can be resolved with bounded evidence.
- **What/where:** read `src/disasm.rs`, `src/analysis.rs`, `src/ir.rs`, and loader mappings; record findings and an exact implementation design in this plan. Use synthetic x86-32/x86-64 pattern candidates first; inspect LE fixup/address limitations without assuming relocated table entries. Select exactly one pattern only if bounds checks, table base, entry width, target executable mapping, and branch semantics can be established from typed decoder facts.
- **Deliverable:** positive and near-miss byte layouts, explicit rejection conditions, maximum 1024 entries/site and 100,000 recovered edges/project as initial caps, direct-versus-inferred provenance, serialization/revision changes, and expected CFG/xref/function-ownership effects. No decoder-text regex inference, whole-memory pointer guessing, or general symbolic execution.
- **Why:** the current known gap is real, but a broad recovery promise would be unsafe and hard to verify.
- **Verify:** design explains every proposed edge and at least five false-positive cases (missing guard, invalid base/width, non-executable target, truncated table, unsupported relocation); record go/no-go. A no-go leaves step 16 blocked/deferred, not implemented speculatively.
- **Depends on:** 6, 8.

### 16. [large] Implement only the proven indirect-jump pattern, conditional on go (P3)
- [ ] Add the approved bounded resolver, or defer after a no-go investigation.
- **What/where:** `src/disasm.rs`, `src/analysis.rs`, `src/db.rs`, new `tests/jump_tables.rs`; `src/lib.rs`/adapters only for agreed evidence fields. Require the exact prerequisites from step 15, keep direct/inferred edge evidence distinct, retain unresolved diagnostics when prerequisites fail, integrate cache replay/revision invalidation, and never modify segment bytes or the original file.
- **Why:** improve CFG completeness without silently inventing control flow. Shared-tail/function ownership limitations remain explicit.
- **Verify:** exact recovered edge/xref sets on the approved positive fixture; every near-miss is unresolved; table/project caps cannot OOM or silently clip inferred graphs (report an explicit diagnostic and leave the site unresolved); fresh/snapshot queries agree; existing direct-flow behavior is unchanged.
- **Depends on:** 7, 15, and a recorded go decision. Priority remains P3; do not count a deliberate deferral as implemented.

### 17. [medium] Publish migration guidance and verify the integrated release (P2)
- [ ] Document delivered features and run the complete configured gate.
- **What/where:** `README.md`, `docs/book/src/cli-reference.md`, `mcp-tools.md`, `json-protocol.md`, `sidecar-format.md`, `architecture.md`, `performance.md`, and `SUMMARY.md` as needed: examples, new tool count/schema revision, old/new `func` response, raw mapping/cache behavior, diagnostic/IR limitations, pattern syntax, annotation conflict policy, and legacy sidecar handling. Do not write user documentation as a history of planning tasks. Update release notes via the established release-plz workflow, not an invented manual version bump.
- **Verify:** run, in order, `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, and `cargo doc --no-deps`; documentation must be warning-free. Run `mdbook build docs/book` in build mode and the manual release workflow benchmark. CLI/MCP capability discovery and examples match executable behavior; no proprietary inputs or sidecars enter tracked files.
- **Depends on:** 3, 5, 7, 8, 10, 12, 14. If step 16 ships in this release, include its tests/docs; otherwise explicitly list it as deferred and do not block the primary release on research.

## Ordering and parallelism

- Start with 1 and 2 in parallel; 4 follows 1. Prioritize 3, 5, 6, and 7 before P2 feature work.
- After the foundation, IR coverage (8), search (9–10), and annotation transfer (11–12) can proceed independently; coordinate shared CLI/MCP and DB files to avoid conflicts.
- Performance 13→14 follows bounded inspection. Research 15→conditional 16 follows diagnostics/IR and is not a blocker for the main release.
- 17 is the integration/documentation release gate. Each feature issue owns its tests; 17 is not a late testing phase.

## Files

These are expected build-mode changes, not changes made during this planning session.

- **Modify:** `src/lib.rs`, `src/loader.rs`, `src/analysis.rs`, `src/db.rs`, `src/disasm.rs` (diagnostic/indirect facts only as needed), `src/ir.rs`, `src/cli.rs`, `src/mcp.rs`; `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` (only if a digest dependency is needed); `tests/stale_cache.rs`, `tests/cli.rs`, `tests/mcp.rs`, `tests/ir.rs`, `tests/addr_hex.rs`, `tests/common/mod.rs` and `tests/fixtures/builders.rs` only for focused fixture support; `README.md`; existing book chapters listed above.
- **Create:** `src/search.rs`, `src/annotations.rs`, `tests/raw_mapping.rs`, `tests/function_pages.rs`, `tests/diagnostics.rs`, `tests/byte_search.rs`, `tests/annotation_transfer.rs`, `tests/mcp_workflow_perf.rs`, `docs/book/src/performance.md`; conditional `tests/jump_tables.rs` after a research go decision.
- **Delete:** none.
- **Keep unchanged:** original analyzed binaries, proprietary `_testdata/`, release automation/CI policy unless a demonstrated integration requirement emerges. No general module split or adjacent refactor.

## Risks

1. **Wrong cache identity or stale annotations:** raw remapping and richer snapshots can mix incompatible address spaces. Guard loader configuration before replay, reject ambiguous mapping changes with annotations, and test legacy sidecars explicitly.
2. **Oversized/untrusted inputs or misleading completeness:** annotation JSON, wildcard scans, diagnostic records, and inferred edges need independent budgets and truthful errors/truncation metadata. Row pagination alone does not bound every transport allocation or CFG export.
3. **False analysis claims and scope creep:** diagnostic absence is not proof; IR mappings are partial; inferred edges require evidence. Benchmark/research decisions may legitimately yield no-go. Do not turn either into a general decompiler or session framework.

## Alternatives considered

- **Expose raw flags first and fix cache identity later** — rejected because the same bytes opened with different architecture/base can reuse incompatible layouts or annotations.
- **Build a resident MCP cache and broad jump-table resolver immediately** — rejected because measured bottlenecks and a reliable conservative pattern are not established. Separate evidence-gathering from conditional implementation.

## Success criteria

- [x] All nine approved proposal areas have detailed issues, concrete acceptance checks, priorities, and dependency ordering; conditional work is clearly marked.
- [ ] Same bytes under different raw mappings never reuse incompatible cached analysis; mapping-mismatched annotation reuse fails without mutation.
- [ ] CLI/MCP raw opens report matching effective architecture/base/entry; defaults remain unchanged.
- [ ] Large-function block/instruction pages reconstruct the exact original sequence within 1024-row page caps; default `func` remains compact.
- [ ] Discovery reasons and diagnostic sites are deterministic, bounded, filterable, and identical after valid snapshot reuse; missing diagnostics are not represented as proof of completeness.
- [ ] IR metadata distinguishes genuine NOP, partial implemented mappings, and unlifted fallback; all five modes have coverage checks.
- [ ] Byte search returns exact overlapping fixture matches and correct offsets without crossing gaps, allocating BSS, or silently exceeding scan limits.
- [ ] Annotation export/import is versioned, identity-checked, bounded, idempotent, and atomic even when the final row fails validation.
- [ ] Repeated-MCP benchmark results and a measured optimization go/no-go are recorded; no unsupported speedup claim.
- [ ] Jump-table investigation records go/no-go; if implemented, every inferred edge is justified and negative fixtures remain unresolved.
- [ ] Breaking response changes and legacy sidecar behavior have tested, executable migration examples.
- [ ] `cargo test` passes; then `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, and warning-free `cargo doc --no-deps` pass.
- [ ] `mdbook build docs/book` succeeds in build mode; no analyzed binary, proprietary fixture, or sidecar is committed.

title: yaxpeax-arm decode panic on hostile ARM32 words aborts instead of Error::Invalid
description:
## Summary

`yaxpeax-arm 0.5.0` panics (`Reg::from_u8: register number out of range`, `armv7.rs:585`) inside `ArmDecoder::decode` on some 4-byte words (e.g. bytes `f9 f0 00 00` as Arm32). Both `disasm_range` and the new `disasm_first` propagate the panic instead of returning `Error::Invalid`, so hostile ARM32 bytes abort the process instead of producing the `{"error": ...}` envelope. Pre-existing (old shrink-window path panicked identically); found via panic-parity assertions in `tests/disasm_first.rs:97-99`.

## Where

- `src/disasm.rs:853` (`decode_single_armv7`): matches only on `Err` from `ArmDecoder::decode`; the `Ok`-path assumption is violated by the inner panic.
- Same root via `disasm_armv7_partial` range path (verified `disasm_range` panics on the same input).
- Callers: `decode_one` (`src/analysis.rs:683`) maps `Error::Invalid` to path-end but cannot catch a panic, so `Project::analyze` on hostile ARM32 input panics.

## Reproduction (verified 2026-10-14, binscout master c32d53f)

```rust
use binscout::disasm::{Arch, disasm_first, disasm_range, DEFAULT_MAX_INSNS};
let bytes = vec![0xF9, 0xF0, 0x00, 0x00];
let _ = disasm_first(Arch::Arm32, &bytes, 0x1000); // panics
let _ = disasm_range(Arch::Arm32, &bytes, 0x1000, DEFAULT_MAX_INSNS); // panics
```

Backtrace (RUST_BACKTRACE=1):

```text
<yaxpeax_arm::armv7::Reg>::from_u8 at yaxpeax-arm-0.5.0/src/armv7.rs:585
<yaxpeax_arm::armv7::InstDecoder as Decoder<ARMv7>>::decode_into at armv7.rs:2162
binscout::disasm::decode_single_armv7 at src/disasm.rs:853
binscout::disasm::disasm_first_arm32 at src/disasm.rs:882
```

Byte-swapped input (`00 00 f0 f9`) correctly returns `Err(Invalid("arm32 decode error ..."))` — only some word patterns trigger the inner panic.

## Fix direction

- Contain the panic at the `yaxpeax-arm` boundary (`std::panic::catch_unwind` in `decode_single_armv7` and the range partial path, mapping panic to `Error::Invalid`), or pre-validate the word patterns that trigger it. Must cover both range and first-instruction paths plus Thumb mode if affected (fuzz all 4-byte words / targeted corpus).
- Equivalence: previously-panicking inputs must become `Error::Invalid` (path end via `decode_one`), all other outputs unchanged. CLI must emit `{"error":...}` exit 1, never abort.

## Acceptance

- Regression tests: panicking word(s) return `Err(Invalid)` via `disasm_range`, `disasm_first`, and `analyze`/CLI without abort; byte-swapped control still errors identically; fuzz corpus over ARM32/Thumb words finds no further panics.
- `tests/disasm_first.rs` panic-parity arms replaced with invalid-error assertions.
- Four gates pass: `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo doc --no-deps`.
close_reason: Contained yaxpeax-arm panics via catch_unwind in decode_single_armv7 + disasm_armv7_partial; hostile words now Error::Invalid. 4 gates green.

title: Performance-focused project review: measured costs and scaling risks
description:
Review of current binscout v0.1.1 on 2026-10-13, not a pending source diff. Structural diff showed no tracked code changes; pre-existing untracked ._dont_add_examples/ was excluded. User approved recording the epic and all 13 proposed issues. No source edits, commits, or pushes authorized/performed.

Verification: cargo test (202 tests passed), cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo fmt --check, cargo doc --no-deps all passed. Release baseline built with cargo build --release --bins; rustc 1.99.0, cargo 1.99.0, ARM64 macOS 27.0.1. Review covered Project/CLI/MCP, persistence, analysis/disassembly/IR, object/LE loading, string extraction and relevant tests. Existing closed rsdbg-jbw.3 covers stats/compaction/small-fixture size checks, not these scaling defects. No open duplicate issues found.

Measurements (end-to-end CLI including process startup, warm filesystem cache; synthetic stress inputs, not representative production estimates): 12 runs/case. Input is N NOP bytes followed by RET, raw x86-64 fallback. At N=100000, median/p95/p99 ms and mean sequential ops/sec: uncached functions --limit 1 = 114.07/126.38/126.38, 8.55 ops/sec; cold analysis+save (load, delete temporary sidecar before each run) = 205.59/244.62/244.62, 4.70 ops/sec; cached functions = 45.00/48.58/48.58, 22.01 ops/sec; cached annotate 0 --comment benchmark = 95.85/107.07/107.07, 10.29 ops/sec. Cached one-row function RSS at 100001 instructions was 55263232 bytes (52.7 MiB). At N=10000, respective medians = 15.66,66.80,23.50,55.94 ms. Twelve observations are insufficient to estimate production tail latency; nearest-rank p95/p99 equal maxima, and the 10k uncached case included a 265.25 ms startup outlier.

900001-instruction stress case: annotate took 0.65s wall (0.36 user,0.17 system) and 1013563392 bytes maximum RSS (966.6 MiB); sidecar logical size after load/annotations was 536875008 bytes. In a separate sampled annotate run, 347/549 samples (63.2%) were in Project::save's db::save subtree; block JSON serialization alone accounted for 122/549 samples. Dense-NOP uncached analysis sample: 625/761 samples in Walker::run's decode_one subtree, including 499/761 samples (65.6%) under the x86 range decoder; observed repeated formatting, vector allocation/reallocation and destruction. Percentages are inclusive stack-sample fractions, not independent additive CPU percentages or whole-process allocation counts.

Stale-cache experiment: query a new one-byte RET file using the 900001-instruction sidecar. Results equal the uncached one-instruction function row. Twelve-run median/p95/p99 = 290.46/399.45/399.45 ms versus 3.07/4.09/4.09 ms with nonexistent sidecar; throughput 3.30 versus 309.54 ops/sec. Single-run RSS = 562954240 versus 5013504 bytes. Cache is deserialized before content-hash comparison.

Many-function stress: bytes 55 48 89 e5 c3 repeated N times. With no sidecar, stats recovered exactly N functions/N blocks/3N instructions. Three-run times: N=1000: 0.0131,0.0109,0.0106s; N=10000: 0.0809,0.0810,0.0821s; N=50000: 0.5881,0.5594,0.5661s. Algorithmic ownership comparison count is validated by source; these are baseline times, not measured optimization gains.

Reproduction commands: E=/Volumes/T7/DeveloperData/cargo-target/release/binscout; D=<temporary directory>. Generate inputs with Python pathlib.Path(D+'/nops-N.bin').write_bytes(b'\x90'*N+b'\xc3') and pathlib.Path(D+'/functions-N.bin').write_bytes(bytes.fromhex('554889e5c3')*N). Run $E --db $D/absent.redb functions $D/nops-N.bin --limit 1; $E --db $D/cache.redb load $D/nops-N.bin; $E --db $D/cache.redb functions $D/nops-N.bin --limit 1; $E --db $D/cache.redb annotate $D/nops-N.bin 0 --comment benchmark. Keep nonexistent DB nonexistent for uncached runs; delete cache before cold-load runs. Use time.perf_counter around subprocess.run(capture_output=True), validate exit zero/JSON, sort observations for nearest-rank quantiles, and divide run count by total elapsed for throughput. Memory command: /usr/bin/time -l $E --db $D/cache.redb annotate $D/nops-N.bin 0 --comment benchmark. Sampling command while workload runs: /usr/bin/sample PID 1 1 -file $D/profile.txt. Artifacts from this audit: /private/var/folders/w9/shn0shjj527fkyfbbbgkfng40000gn/T/opencode/binscout-perf-vdojbuq0/{cpu-sample.txt,annotation-sample.txt,owner-sample.txt}; temporary paths are not persistent benchmark infrastructure.

Instrumentation limits: samply unavailable, xctrace unavailable because full Xcode is not installed. Used /usr/bin/sample and /usr/bin/time -l; no complete allocation-count or I/O-byte profile captured. Allocator and pread/pwrite/flush stacks corroborate costs but do not quantify all allocations/I/O. Do not claim before/after speedups until fixes are benchmarked on realistic binaries and stress cases.

Lower-confidence/further investigation (not blockers proven by these measurements): MCP opens/reconstructs Project for every request and holds one global mutex (src/mcp.rs:17-27,174-193,208-398), so unrelated binaries serialize; measure MCP request sequences/concurrency before proposing bounded caching/per-project scheduling, preserve redb exclusivity and cross-process annotation/file freshness. Loader independently owns segment and section buffers (separate mapped-byte budgets); shared backing would change public Vec APIs. Mach-O dependency parsing allocates tables before project cap checks. LE pads/truncates pages without releasing capacity, has separate object/fixup budgets and inconsistent truncation/count policies. Public raw-mapping options and analysis-version cache validity deserve a separate correctness review. These follow-ups require focused profiling/reproduction and are not promised speedups.

Optimization discipline: one lever per change; golden JSON/analysis equality and differential tests, including overlap/order/error semantics, before claiming equivalence. Security budgets deliberately introduce rejection behavior and must be specified as contract changes. Suggested first work: fix zero-fill panic and ineffective allocation caps, then measured persistence/cache costs and quadratic ownership. Benchmark/regression suite currently has no criterion/divan or equivalent performance coverage. Add stable synthetic workloads and allocation/instruction-count guardrails alongside realistic inputs; avoid flaky wall-clock assertions in ordinary tests.

Completion requires addressing each child (or explicit accepted-risk decision), release before/after measurements, differential output checks and the four normal project gates.

Where: src/lib.rs:362-365 (Project::bytes_at). After finding a segment by mem_size, have = data.len().saturating_sub(off).min(len) becomes zero when off > data.len(), but data[off..off+have] still panics. This violates documented zero-padding behavior, CLI JSON error/result contract, and can disrupt MCP request execution. CWE-248/400; local user/tool-selected input, not demonstrated remote compromise.
Reproduced with release CLI: copy tests/fixtures/pe32-basic.exe to a temporary file; read e_lfanew at 0x3c, optional-header size at pe+20, first section header at pe+24+optional_size; set first section VirtualSize (header+8) to 0x400 while raw size remains 0x200. Run binscout --db <absent temporary DB> disasm <copy> 0x401300 1. Actual: exit 101, empty stdout, stderr panic at src/lib.rs:365: range start index 768 out of range for slice of length 512.
Fix: perform the copy only when have > 0 (or bounded source get); keep initialized zeros for bytes wholly past file data. Preserve mixed file/zero ranges and mapped-range validation. This restores the promised behavior rather than optimizing it. Never mutate checked-in fixtures or analyzed inputs.
acceptance_criteria: Add synthetic integration tests for wholly zero-filled tail, off exactly at data.len(), off beyond data.len(), mixed file/zero range and unmapped range. bytes_at must return correct zeros without panicking; CLI disasm/ir must emit valid JSON with documented exit behavior, and MCP must remain responsive. Run all four project gates.
close_reason: Fixed bytes_at zero-tail panic (have>0 guard) + tests/bytes_tail.rs 6 tests; 4 gates green

title: Provide first-instruction decoding without discarding window results
description:
Where: src/analysis.rs:639-657; src/disasm.rs:506-577. decode_one decodes entire x86 windows, retries shrinking windows on trailing errors, removes first instruction and discards remaining formatted/allocated instructions. Dense one-byte code can decode roughly 15 instructions per retained instruction. Bounded O(N) overhead, not quadratic.
Measured dense-NOP release profile: 900001-instruction input; 625/761 samples in decode_one subtree and 499/761 (65.6%) under x86 range disassembly; allocation/reallocation, formatter/split_asm and dropping unused Insn vectors prominent. This is stress-specific, not a typical binary hotspot percentage.
Fix: shared internal first-instruction decoder or streaming visitor, reusing identical iced decoder/formatter options and existing Insn conversion; retain existing public range/partial APIs. Decode only requested first instruction, not the trailing window. Consider formatter/buffer reuse only as separate performance lever.
Equivalence: valid first instruction output (addr/bytes/mnemonic/operands/branch and memory targets) must equal original shrinking-window algorithm; trailing invalid bytes cannot alter that first result. ISA/truncation/cap/error semantics need differential oracle, not assumed equality.
acceptance_criteria: Differential first-instruction output/error tests on generated windows and all fixtures, including invalid/truncated first opcode, valid first opcode with invalid tail, prefixes and all supported ISAs. Analysis functions/CFG/xrefs/golden JSON unchanged. Before/after CPU/allocation profiles and realistic/dense-NOP release benchmarks; four gates pass.
close_reason: Fixed: decode_one now uses shared disasm_first single-step decoder. Gates pass.

title: Replace LE import Vec membership scans with an identity index
description:
Where: src/loader.rs:418-444,490-495. Each import-producing LE fixup constructs owned library/name fields then uses imports.contains(&imp). U unique imports cost U*(U-1)/2 equality comparisons (~five billion at 100000 cap); repeats can cause O(F*U) scans across up to two million fixups. This runs in load_le conversion before Project::load_or_raw rejects LE (src/lib.rs:725-730), and public loader callers can invoke directly. Source-validated, no runtime stress profile yet.
Fix: keep output vector for first-seen order, add keyed membership index matching resulting ImportRef equality, not numeric module identity alone. Preserve exact break at unique-output cap and all ordinal/name/unresolved/demangle fields. Different module indices may decode to same name; real library names can equal fallback mod#N. Use a keyed DoS-resistant hash index or ordered set, not predictable collision-prone hashing for hostile names.
Equivalence: index membership equals existing equality predicate and vector insertion order remains first occurrence. Early Project LE rejection is a separate possible optimization; do not conflate with public loader behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Golden/differential ordered imports for mixed ordinal/name fixups, repeated records, duplicate library names at distinct indices, fallback-name collisions and cap boundaries. Benchmark unique and heavily duplicate inputs using public loader path; show nonquadratic membership scaling and unchanged results/error policy. Four gates pass.
close_reason: HashSet LeImportKey dedup index preserving order/equality; tests/le_import_dedup.rs 6 tests; nonquadratic scaling shown; 4 gates green

title: Specify and enforce input plus aggregate metadata memory budgets
description:
Where: src/lib.rs:122-125; src/loader.rs:218-225,323-335,355-385,498-535. Project fully reads/hashes file before loader limits; huge raw input can allocate before rejection. Segment/section data caps do not cover section/import/export/library names, repeated decoded names or demangled output. Count caps allow large referenced names copied repeatedly; object parsing can allocate before returned-table caps. CWE-400/770, local input/stdio tool trust boundary; no measured malicious OOM or remote exposure asserted.
Fix: define separate input policy and aggregate owned-metadata/output budgets, then enforce before reading/copying/demangling where possible. Read from one opened file with bounded streaming/checked accumulation rather than relying only on a racy metadata stat. Do not simply apply MAX_MAPPED_BYTES to container file length: unmapped overlays/debug data are currently accepted. Repeated-name/demangle caching can reduce work but does not bound public owned output copies.
Contract caveat: security budgets necessarily introduce new rejection behavior and are not fully output-isomorphic. Agree on limits and error precedence; oversize must return Error::Limit, not be interpreted as invalid container and fall back raw. Persisted snapshots also require explicit row/aggregate budget consideration.
acceptance_criteria: Specify independently justified input/metadata/output limits and compatibility policy. Tests at exact boundaries and over limits, shared long ELF section/symbol names, replacement-character decoding expansion, large unmapped overlays and checked read-growth behavior. Assert bounded memory before copying/parsing and CLI/MCP error propagation without raw fallback; include snapshot path budget decisions. Four gates pass.
close_reason: Fixed: input/metadata/snapshot budgets enforced, Error::Limit without raw fallback. Gates pass.

title: Keep LE length-prefixed names inside their declared tables
description:
Where: src/loader/le.rs:650-667 (parse_names). Initial start/end range is checked but each length-prefixed name is sliced against full file, not table end. A final name can consume bytes in the following table. Rust file slice remains bounds checked: this is malformed-table acceptance/cross-table confusion, not demonstrated unsafe memory access.
Source-derived example: bytes [5,88,3,97,98,99], first table range 0..2. Name length 5 consumes following table bytes while staying in file; a second procedure table starting at 2 can independently interpret abc. Reachable via public LE parser and parsing before Project LE rejection. No runtime reproduction performed in this audit.
Fix: create bounded bytes[start..end] cursor or checked name-end <= end test for every record, including ordinal trailer if this table format has one. Preserve all valid names/order; cross-boundary malformed inputs should return Error::Invalid (Project recognized-LE mapping must remain explicit unsupported, never raw fallback).
acceptance_criteria: Tests for names ending exactly at table boundary, crossing into next table while within file, zero length/empty table, truncated length/data/trailer and EOF. Full valid LE fixtures unchanged; malformed public parser inputs fail without panic, and Project/CLI recognized-LE errors remain explicit. Four gates pass.
close_reason: parse_names table-bound check returning Invalid on cross-boundary; 6 tests in tests/loader_le.rs; regression pinned; 4 gates green

title: Bound string candidates before allocating and sorting all hits
description:
Where: src/loader/strings.rs:119-124,164-169,191-205. extract scans ASCII/UTF16LE/UTF16BE and creates every owned StringHit before sort/truncate(max_hits); max_hits=0 still allocates/scans. Default 10000-hit cap is therefore not an intermediate-memory cap. A permitted 256 MiB buffer repeating AAAA followed by 0xff yields approximately 53.7 million ASCII candidates; this is source-derived amplification, not an executed OOM test. CWE-400/770.
Fix: lazily discover run descriptors per encoding, merge by file offset and select capped hits before decoding owned strings. Preserve equal-offset order ASCII then LE then BE (existing append order plus stable sort), all threshold/alignment/EOF behavior and resulting addresses. Counting bounds before constructing UTF16 text also removes allocations for rejected short runs. Do not just stop after max_hits ASCII hits: earlier UTF16 hits may displace them. Retained individual strings can remain large; total output-byte budgets are a separate policy change.
Equivalence proof: merge the same ordered candidate populations using the same tie-break, select the same sorted prefix, decode unchanged selected spans. Full allocation profiling still required.
acceptance_criteria: Differentially compare old/reference extraction with new output on generated small buffers across caps (including zero), minimum lengths, both endians, odd offsets/lengths, EOF and equal-offset ties. Benchmark dense short-run stress with small caps and count allocations/peak memory to verify intermediate owned-hit count is bounded. Preserve extraction output exactly and pass four gates.
close_reason: Bound string candidates via lazy run-merge + tests/strings_bound.rs 9 tests; 4 gates green

title: Enforce ARM seed budget during candidate collection
description:
Where: src/analysis.rs:737-748,773-834. ARM/AArch64/Thumb branches append all prologue candidates before global sorting/deduplication/selection under MAX_SEEDS; instruction/function caps act later. Dense matching words after an initial return can leave round-one traversal small but candidate collection huge. For 256 MiB raw input, source-derived u64 payload alone can approach 512 MiB for AArch64 or 1 GiB for Thumb; these are theoretical bounds, not measured OOM results. CWE-400/770.
Fix: bounded/lazy globally ordered candidate streams merged across segments, enforcing the 100000 accepted-seed budget without collecting every address. Preserve sorting, duplicate handling, reached/undecodable exclusions, segment order independence and existing wrapping semantics. Simply stopping after 100000 raw candidates is not equivalent because rejected candidates consume no accepted slots.
Proof obligation: emitted seeds equal the original sorted/deduped, reached-filtered, decodable prefix. If rejecting instead of preserving prefix, specify the changed contract explicitly.
acceptance_criteria: Differential seed/output tests with out-of-order and overlapping segments, duplicate addresses, early reached/undecodable candidates, wrapped mappings and over-cap candidate counts across all ARM variants. Allocation-instrumented dense-prologue stress must show bounded candidate storage while preserving accepted seeds. Normal four gates pass.
close_reason: ARM seeds via lazy k-way heap merge under MAX_SEEDS + tests/arm_seed_budget.rs 7 tests; 4 gates green

title: Use logarithmic predecessor lookup for function ownership
description:
Where: src/analysis.rs:972-978; ownership calls at 1054,1085,1103. entry_list.iter().rfind(|e| **e <= va) reverse-scans sorted entries for each block/edge. Complexity O(B*F) instead of predecessor lookup O(B log F). Repeating raw x86-64 bytes 55 48 89 e5 c3 100000 times produces 100000 functions/blocks and 300000 instructions within caps; ownership assignment alone permits 5000050000 predicates.
Measured baseline for identical-pattern uncached stats: 1000 functions ~0.011s,10000 ~0.081s,50000 ~0.566s (three runs each). No before/after speedup measured.
Fix: entry_list.partition_point(|e| *e <= va), choose preceding index, preserving fallback to first entry when address is below first. A monotonic sweep can separately optimize sorted block assignment but do not combine levers in the first patch.
Equivalence: sorted entries plus partition_point identifies exactly the greatest entry <= va; explicit fallback matches current rfind(None). No change to gap ownership or ordering.
acceptance_criteria: Differential owner tests below first, exactly at entries, in gaps, above last and generated address sets. Golden functions/CFG/callgraph equality for many-function fixtures; benchmark 1k/10k/50k/100k release workloads and show lookup comparison/scaling improvement. Pass four gates.
close_reason: function_owner partition_point + 3 tests; 18-565x speedup; 4 gates green

title: Index string spans while preserving first overlapping match
description:
Where: src/analysis.rs:1131-1166,especially 1160-1166. Each data reference linearly finds its target among string spans: O(D*S). A raw x86-32 mapping with 100000 push-imm32 references to mapped zero padding and 10000 printable strings can cause one billion failed interval comparisons within existing caps. This is source-validated complexity, not an executed latency measurement.
Fix: retain the sorted span order and build prefix maximum end addresses. Find the first prefix max > target and ensure its index lies before the upper bound of starts <= target; return the corresponding first matching span. Handles overlaps unlike a naive last-start predecessor lookup. Use checked/wrapping behavior consistent with current endpoints.
Equivalence: first prefix reaching end>target is the earliest span with that property; the starts upper bound enforces start<=target, preserving the current first-match interval selection. Prefix build O(S), queries O(log S). Alternative interval index must explicitly preserve first-match semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Differential reference-link tests for misses, starts, exclusive ends, duplicate starts, nested/overlapping intervals, segment overlap and wrapped endpoints; complete xref ordering/kinds/targets unchanged. Release benchmark many missed refs against many spans, with output equality and comparison-count evidence; four gates pass.
close_reason: StringSpanIndex prefix-max + tests/string_spans.rs 8 tests (~55x release); 4 gates green

title: Update annotations without rewriting unchanged analysis snapshot
description:
Where: src/lib.rs:307-319,330-336; src/db.rs:392-403,454-472. rename_function/set_comment call Project::save; db::save deletes all seven tables and rewrites every instruction/xref/string for a one-row annotation change. Cost scales with full analysis, including b.insns.clone(), JSON encoding, redb writes and durable commit.
Measured release stress: 900001 NOP/RET instructions, annotate 0 --comment profile = 0.65s wall and 1013563392 bytes maximum RSS; sidecar after load/annotations 536875008 bytes. Sampled run has 347/549 samples in snapshot save subtree, including 122/549 block JSON serialization samples. At 100001 instructions cached annotate median 95.85ms vs cached one-row functions 45.00ms (12 runs). Snapshot saving is a measured bottleneck; improvement not yet measured.
Fix: annotation-only transaction for a matching persisted snapshot, insert/delete only changed annotation row; preserve full snapshot creation when none exists and full save after content mismatch/reanalysis. Preserve immediate durability, clearing semantics, rename-known-entry validation, annotations across changed binaries, and redb exclusivity. Avoid persisting an annotation against the wrong snapshot if another process changed sidecar; validate transaction metadata as needed.
Equivalence: when analysis identity matches durable snapshot, only annotation differs; modifying that row produces the same logical snapshot as full rewrite without changing analysis tables. Fresh/stale snapshots take the original bootstrap path. Annotate with both flags may need batching as a separate scoped change.
acceptance_criteria: Tests compare reopened logical analysis/annotations against full-save reference for rename/comment/set/clear, fresh DB, changed binary, unrelated annotations and failure paths. Verify unchanged analysis tables are not rewritten for matched snapshot, immediate persistence and binary bytes untouched. Profile release annotation latency/RSS/write bytes before/after on 100k/900k stress plus real binaries; four gates pass.
close_reason: Annotation-only save_annotation/persist_annotation + tests/annotation_fast.rs 9 tests; 4 gates green

title: Skip stale snapshot decoding after metadata mismatch
description:
Where: src/lib.rs:129-136,139-156; src/db.rs:507-631. open_inner calls db::load (decode all records and rebuild graphs) before comparing content_hash. On mismatch all decoded analysis is discarded; only annotations are retained.
Measured: one-byte RET input with sidecar of 900001-instruction input yields same one-function row as absent-sidecar query. Twelve-run stale median/p95/p99 = 290.46/399.45/399.45ms vs 3.07/4.09/4.09ms absent; single-run RSS 562954240 vs 5013504 bytes. Stale results are not saved by read command, so cost repeats on every query.
Fix: read/validate snapshot metadata first; on hash mismatch load required annotations but do not deserialize obsolete analysis; on match load full analysis as today. Prefer one coherent read transaction to avoid metadata/snapshot races.
Equivalence caveat: current implementation errors on corrupt stale analysis before reanalysis. Skipping that decoding changes error behavior for corrupt mismatched snapshots. Explicitly document whether stale derived cache corruption can be discarded or preserve validation via a separate policy; do not claim strict all-input equivalence. Healthy stale snapshots should yield identical analysis/annotations.
acceptance_criteria: Test cache hit/miss, missing tables/versions, healthy stale snapshot annotation carryover, stale corrupt-row policy and transaction consistency. Benchmark changed-small-input/large-old-cache vs absent cache; allocation/RSS must not scale with discarded instruction rows. No read-path save; golden healthy outputs equal; four gates pass.
close_reason: Metadata-first load_cached with Stale snapshot path + read-only opens; tests/stale_cache.rs 14 tests; 4 gates green on combined tree

title: Reuse a lazily compiled matcher per string-search query
description:
Where: src/analysis.rs:524-539 and src/loader/strings.rs:90-103 (Regex::new at 99-102). Every eligible string calls matches_pattern which compiles regex again. Cost = eligible hits times regex compilation plus matching. Pattern-length limit does not bound compile count. Source-validated; no isolated timing/compilation profile yet.
Fix: query-local matcher initialized once lazily at first row reaching pattern evaluation; reuse for eligible rows. Keep substring and case sensitivity semantics. Eager compilation changes current behavior: malformed/overlong patterns return successful empty result when no hit survives earlier section/min_len filters; retain that behavior unless a separate contract change is approved.
Equivalence: same compiled regex and same per-row predicate, same point at which errors become observable; output order/paging unchanged. Do not combine with paging-allocation changes.
acceptance_criteria: Count/instrument regex compilation: at most once per query with eligible hits, zero for no eligible hits. Tests for valid/bad/overlong patterns, no rows/all rows prefiltered, limit zero, beyond-end offset, substring and explicit regex modes. Benchmark thousands of eligible rows; four gates pass.
close_reason: Per-query lazy PatternMatcher reuse (1 compile/query); tests/strings_matcher.rs 7 + 2 unit; ~55x on 3000-row bench; 4 gates green

title: Avoid cloning whole result sets for paged queries
description:
Where: src/analysis.rs:415-429,433-452,469-475,521-546. Function/block page helpers build every summary then clone selected page; xref helpers materialize all matches; filtered string query clones all matches including text before paging. Returned page cap 1024 does not bound intermediate result allocation. Filtered strings is production CLI/MCP path; function/block/xref Analysis page helpers currently have no production callers found, so prioritize strings. Source-validated, not independently allocation-profiled.
Fix: construct/clone only selected page after filtering. Preserve necessary evaluation of patterns past selected page where existing error semantics demand it (especially zero-limit/no-eligible behavior); this is separate from matcher compilation reuse. For infallible helpers use skip/take before summary construction and cloning; avoid overflow in offset calculations.
Equivalence: identical predicate and storage-order sequence followed by identical bounded page; defer materialization only. Preserve Option None vs empty result semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Differential page tests for all offsets/limits including zero, oversized cap, beyond end and extreme usize offsets; empty sets, filter interactions and invalid-pattern error behavior unchanged. Allocation tests show owned strings/summaries scale with returned page not matches; release benchmark large match population/small page. Four gates pass.
close_reason: Fixed: paged helpers skip/take before summary construction; filtered strings clone only selected page. Gates pass.
